summary: Sustained 5xx spike during large embedding upload causing accept-queue collapse and runtime preemption
description:
Issue summary:
Customer QueryFlow reported a sustained elevation in 5xx responses (~8-12% error rate) beginning 2026-03-13 03:20 UTC during a large embedding ingestion job. Errors manifested as 502/503 from API gateway with upstream runtime disconnects and occasional runtime GPU preemptions.

Impact:
- QueryFlow dedicated tenant experienced failed embedding batches (10-20% of batches failing) and increased tail latency for chat calls.
- Customer reported retry storms and billing disputes for failed uploads.
- Incident observed primarily in us-west-2; spillover traces in us-east-1 for cross-region prefetch.

Environment:
- prod, dedicated capacity pool: dp-dedicated-42, node type: a100-80gb equivalent
- Ingress: api-gw-v3 (http2 multiplexing enabled), runtime: inference-runtime-v1.28
- Affected models: redwood-embed-v2 (batching for embedding), llama-2-7b-chat (mixed chat traffic)

Steps to reproduce (customer):
1) Start large CSV-to-embeddings pipeline with 1,000-5,000 concurrent small payloads using chunked multipart upload (parallelism 40).
2) Simultaneously run streaming chat workload with long-lived connections/keepalives (50 streams).
3) Observe elevated 5xx rate on embedding upload route and intermittent 502s on chat.

Observed logs / snippets (sanitized):
- api-gateway: "2026-03-13T03:22:11Z ERROR upstream reset by peer: connection reset while writing"
- runtime: "[watchdog] GPU preempt event: dev=0 pid=4721 reason=page_fault_retry"
- ingress: "accept_queue_drops=312 backlog=1024 conn_open=512"
comments: 2026-03-13 03:45 UTC - Ava Chen (Support): Initial triage and acknowledged to customer. Asked for request IDs, sample payload, and approximate start time. Escalated to SRE.

2026-03-13 04:10 UTC - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Noted accept_queue growth on api-gw in us-west-2 correlating with customer's start time. Socket backlog saturated; observed large number of half-open chunked uploads. Temporarily increased accept backlog on affected frontends to see immediate effect.

2026-03-13 04:28 UTC - QueryFlow (Customer): Provided request IDs and a sample of the multipart upload payload (14MB average per bundle) and confirmed parallelism of 40 workers. Reported intermittent success after retries but overall high failure rate.

2026-03-13 05:05 UTC - Support (Ava): Notified customer of temporary mitigation (reduced ingress concurrency and chunk size guidance). Opened linked issue with runtime team for GPU preempt investigation.

2026-03-13 11:12 UTC - Runtime Eng (Leila Kaur): Found evidence of KV cache thrashing on dedicated nodes when embedding prefetch and chat KV warms co-occurred; eviction storms led to slower responses and higher OOM likelihood under heavy batching.

2026-03-14 02:30 UTC - Miguel Alvarez (SRE): Implemented transient rate-limiting rule for chunked embedding route for this tenant and increased autoscaler headroom for dp-dedicated-42. Monitoring shows 5xx rate reduced to ~1.2% post-mitigation.
2026-03-14 09:00 UTC - Ava Chen (Support): Updated customer with mitigation and next steps. Customer confirmed improved success rate and agreed to staged rollout of guidance and fixes.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: High parallel multipart embedding uploads created many half-open connections and filled front-end accept queues, causing proxy backpressure and upstream resets.
Hypothesis 2: Concurrent long-lived streaming connections increased kernel/thread pressure; combined with large embedding batches this caused runtime preempt events and GPU pagefault retry cycles.

Evidence: Accept queue metrics (accept_queue_drops) spiked concurrent with customer's job start. Runtime logs show repeated GPU preempt events and KV cache eviction spikes. No immediate code-level regressions found in runtime v1.28 in our initial review.

Telemetry: trace samples attached to related_confluence_pages show increased latency and retries for requests with header 'x-tenant: queryflow' and chunked content-type. Kernel-level stats show fd usage approaching node limits on frontends.

Temporary mitigation validation: Accept backlog increase and targeted rate-limit for chunked uploads for tenant reduced queue depth and lowered 5xx rate; autoscaler headroom reduced runtime preempt frequency.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-14 02:30 UTC): tenant-scoped rate limit for chunked-multipart embedding route; recommended customer reduce parallelism from 40 to 8 and lower per-bundle size to <5MB while we roll permanent fixes.

Short-term fixes planned: increase OS fd and accept_queue tuning on ingress fleet for dedicated pools; add guardrails in api-gateway to detect bursty chunked-multipart patterns and fail fast with guidance headers instead of saturating accept queue.

Medium-term engineering changes: runtime team to address KV cache eviction policy under mixed embedding+streaming workloads; autoscaler to prewarm GPUs for large embedding ingestion patterns and avoid preempt thrash.

Follow-ups: Billing team to review failed batch charges with QueryFlow and offer credit for clearly failed uploads; Solutions Engineering to provide a recommended ingestion pattern (parallelism, chunk size, backoff).
Owner for permanent fixes: Leila Kaur (Runtime Eng) and Miguel Alvarez (SRE). Target ETA for rollout of kernel/tuning changes: 2026-03-28.
